<question>
Can a tenant sublet or hand over the lease in Spain, Colombia and Dubai?
</question>

<answer>
In all three jurisdictions the landlord's consent is needed [1][2][3].

Spain: the tenant cannot assign the contract without the landlord's written consent. A dwelling can be sublet only in part, and only with the landlord's prior written consent [1].

Colombia: the tenant cannot assign or sublet unless the landlord expressly authorises it. If the landlord does authorise it, the landlord may end the contract and demand the property, or sign a new contract with the actual occupants [2].

Dubai: unless the parties agree otherwise, the tenant may not assign the use of the property or sublet it to third parties without the landlord's written consent [3].
</answer>

<reference>
In all three the landlord's consent is needed. Spain: the tenant cannot assign the contract without the landlord's written consent, and a dwelling can be sublet only in part and with the landlord's prior written consent (art. 8 of the Ley de Arrendamientos Urbanos). Colombia: the tenant cannot assign or sublet unless the landlord expressly authorises it, and if he does, the landlord may end the contract and demand the property or sign a new one with the actual occupants (art. 17 of Ley 820 de 2003). Dubai: unless the parties agree otherwise, the tenant may not assign the use of the property or sublet it to third parties without the landlord's written consent (art. 24 of Law No. (26) of 2007).
</reference>
